workPackageTitle: Run result manifest and success/failure/abandon settlement model
notes: Entries are added before implementation and are never renumbered (docs/technical/91-verification-strategy.md § Verification registry). Every entry below was authored before the production code it names.

'status' takes exactly one of 'registered', 'implemented', 'retired' (doc 91 § Entry status). 'evidenceKinds' is read against 'status' (doc 91 § What evidenceKinds means): for a 'registered' entry the list is evidence the verification will produce once built, and nothing may treat it as produced.
The structural validator for this file is owned by TASK-FND-009-002. Until it lands, the shape here matches tests/verification/PLY-001.json exactly.

This file is deliberately NOT named SIM-0*.json. tests/MechaMiner.Simulation.Tests/Support/NegativeControlCoverageTests.cs globs 'SIM-0*.json' and asserts a totals line accounting for every entry across those seven files, so adding an entry to one of them from another work package would break an unrelated package's gate.

Negative controls for these entries are recorded in tests/verification/M3-negative-controls.md. No automated gate asserts that document's coverage: the existing coverage gate (NegativeControlCoverageTests) is scoped to the seven SIM registries and its partition arithmetic is over those files only. That is stated here so a reader does not assume an enforcement that does not exist.

This slice implements the two outcomes a run can reach without a new command: Survived at the 35:00 boundary and Destroyed when Hull reaches zero. The abandon outcome docs/110:289 also assigns to this package needs a voluntary-abandonment command that no package has built, so RunOutcome has no Abandoned member: a member nothing can produce would be a claim that something can.

The settlement itself - what a profile keeps - is not implemented. This slice mines only common ore, which docs/40:90 makes run-local and lost when the run ends regardless of outcome, so both outcomes discard the same thing and no banking decision is observable yet. Hyper Gold banking (docs/40:127, TR-PRG-005) is PST-004's and MIN-002's and has no entry here.
VER-PRG-006-001 is the successor to the retired VER-PLY-001-010, whose claim was that EvaluateTerminalBoundary decides nothing.

entries.summary: The run ends, once, and the two outcomes are distinguishable: phase 13 assigns Destroyed on the tick Hull reaches zero, EvaluateTerminalBoundary assigns Survived when the 35:00 boundary is reached with no result yet assigned, a result already assigned is never replaced, and the published snapshot's terminal flag follows the assignment.

Settling the run stops it without a technical failure: a run destroyed inside a tick still commits that tick, the driver's terminal-transition bridge raises the one-way pause reason between steps, later steps report blocked rather than running a tick, and the host records no technical failure.
